thread:
priyanka (se): hi team — customer onboarding of Redwood Private failing. Agent pods start but never establish TLS to control plane, logs show 'connect: connection refused'. This started after they applied a strict NetworkPolicy. Can we triage?

sara (support): thanks. can you paste the agent pod logs and the netpol that was applied? also which CNI + k8s version?

priyanka (se): cluster: EKS 1.24, calico v3.25, nodes in private subnets behind NAT gateway. netpol applied to namespace 'redwood' is below:
```yaml
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: deny-egress-default
  namespace: redwood
spec:
  podSelector: {}
  policyTypes:
  - Egress
  egress: 
  - to:
    - ipBlock:
        cidr: 10.0.0.0/8
    ports:
    - protocol: UDP
      port: 53
```

priyanka (se): they intended to allow just cluster internal DNS but forgot to allow control plane or internet egress. agent logs:
```
2025-09-02T12:03:15Z agent | dialing control.redwood.ai:443
2025-09-02T12:03:15Z agent | dial tcp 10.2.3.45:443: connect: connection refused
2025-09-02T12:03:15Z agent | will retry in 5s
```

ken (eng): a couple of things to check quickly: 1) networkpolicy only allows what you explicitly permit — FQDNs won't work. 2) agent needs egress to cluster DNS (UDP 53), to the control plane IPs (443), and to any KMS/HSM endpoints if they're using KMS. run from inside the agent container: `curl -v https://control.redwood.ai:443` and `dig @10.96.0.10 control.redwood.ai`

priyanka (se): ran curl from pod -> `curl: (7) Failed to connect to control.redwood.ai port 443: Connection refused`
openssl s_client -connect control.redwood.ai:443 --timeout 5 -> nothing, connection resets. dig to cluster DNS succeeded: `; <<>> DiG 9.11.3 <<>> @10.96.0.10 control.redwood.ai
;; ANSWER: 1`

ops-bot: note: control.redwood.ai resolved to 54.198.23.100 and 3.120.45.12 for customer cluster geo.

infra-bot: quick host-level test: on a node, try `curl -v --interface <node-ip> https://control.redwood.ai:443` to verify node egress. If node-level egress works but pod doesn't, netpol is the culprit. Also check `iptables -t nat -S` and `calicoctl get networkpolicy -o yaml` if using Calico policy.

priyanka (se): did node curl from host -> success, TLS handshake ok and cert verifies. `curl https://control.redwood.ai` from node returns 200. So node can reach control plane but pod cannot.

sara (support): that matches a pod-level NetworkPolicy blocking egress to the control plane CIDRs. Because the netpol you pasted only allows 10.0.0.0/8 UDP 53, all other egress gets denied. Two remediation options: A) add explicit egress rules to allow TCP 443 to Redwood control plane CIDRs and to any managed services (KMS, metrics endpoints) B) remove default-deny while onboarding. Example patch to allow control plane and DNS: 
```bash
kubectl apply -f - <<'YAML'
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: allow-redwood-egress
  namespace: redwood
spec:
  podSelector: {}
  policyTypes:
  - Egress
  egress:
  - to:
    - ipBlock:
        cidr: 10.96.0.0/12 # cluster DNS range
    ports:
    - protocol: UDP
      port: 53
  - to:
    - ipBlock:
        cidr: 54.198.23.100/32 # control.redwood.ai (example)
    ports:
    - protocol: TCP
      port: 443
YAML
```

ken (eng): note: if customer's control plane is behind a NAT gateway or proxy, you should allow the NAT gateway's egress IPs/CIDR too. Also confirm if there's an HTTP proxy doing TLS intercept — that would cause x509 errors (not this case though).

priyanka (se): applied allow-redwood-egress and re-created the agent pods. agent now connects and shows Ready. logs: `connected to control.redwood.ai:443; certificate OK`

priyanka (se): followup: customer asked for a minimal list of CIDRs/ports to allow. they want to lock down egress but keep onboarding working.

sara (support): recommended minimal checklist to give customer: 1) Allow UDP 53 -> cluster DNS IP (10.96.0.10) 2) Allow TCP 443 -> Redwood control plane CIDRs (we provided sample list in customer onboarding doc) 3) If using KMS, allow egress to the KMS endpoints (region-specific) 4) Allow TLS to time sync / NTP if hosts require it (UDP 123) 5) If using a NAT gateway, include its public IPs in allowed egress. Link: https://docs.redwood.ai/private/network-requirements (cc @ken for exact CIDR list) :thumbsup: 

ken (eng): I'll follow up with exact control plane CIDRs per-region and a short runbook to patch netpols safely (canary apply, watch agent logs). If customer wants we can provide a sample MutatingWebhook to add an egress-allow annotation to redwood pods so customers can keep strict defaults for other apps.

priyanka (se): thanks — customer confirmed they can proceed. closing for now.

sara (support): marking resolved, will attach onboarding doc link and the netpol snippet to the ticket and include the CIDR list once Ken posts it. :white_check_mark:
